newsitem.title: UK: UK watchdog stops greyhound collective investment.
newsitem.headline: UK watchdog stops greyhound collective investment.

text.p: Racing greyhounds are a collective investment and must be authorised and licensed as such, according to the Securities and Investments Board (SIB), the overall regulator for financial services in the UK.

SIB on Wednesday obtained a High Court injunction to restrain Anderson Churchill Ltd (ACL) from conducting investment business in the UK, and in particular from operating greyhound bloodstock investment services.
Under the ACL scheme, investors were invited to join greyhound syndicates and to participate in the profits made in the management and racing of greyhounds.

But the Financial Services Act 1986 rules that the operation of a collective investment scheme constitutes investment business and under Section 3 of the Act, no person shall conduct investment business unless authorised or exempted.
SIB argued the ACL arrangement constituted a collective investment scheme. The proceedings brought include a claim for restitution of funds for investors.
